answers.explanation: They're also called services or subsystems.
Some do their job at startup and exit; others run until shutdown.
They run in user context, as ordinary processes.
Disk checking, process scheduling, error logging, and printing are the examples.
Others stay running from boot to shutdown.
Applications don't pertain to the system itself.
They're run by users to solve users' problems.
The trailing d is the daemon naming convention; sshd accepts secure-shell connections.
